_note: Questions for both forms. Edit freely — the app renders whatever is here. Types: radio, checkbox, text, textarea, matrix. Add `other: true` to a radio/checkbox to append an 'Other' free-text option.

feedback.title: How did that go?
feedback.intro: Five questions, about two minutes. Blunt is more useful than polite — we would rather hear what did not work.
feedback.thanks: Thank you — that is genuinely useful.

questions.label: Did you understand what needed attention, without anyone explaining it?
What evidence would you want before you trusted a recommendation like this?
questions.placeholder: What would need to be true for you to act on it?

questions.label: Was anything confusing, or did you get stuck anywhere?
questions.placeholder: Which screen, and what happened? Blank is fine if nothing did.

questions.label: Would you put your own property data into something like this?
What did you expect to be able to do that you could not?
questions.placeholder: The thing you went looking for and did not find.

questionnaire.title: Property / Strata Management Validation Questionnaire
questionnaire.intro: I am building a property intelligence tool for strata and condo communities and property managers, and I want to validate the real problems before building too much. About 4 minutes. Anything marked optional can be skipped without spoiling the answers.
questionnaire.thanks: Thank you — this is exactly the input I need.

questions.label: Which best describes you?
Approximately how many properties or buildings do you deal with?
What are the top 3 things that are hardest to keep track of for a property or building?
questions.help: Documents, maintenance, inspections, assets, deadlines, bylaws, vendors, projects, budgets, reserve planning. Three words each is fine.

questions.label: How confident are you that important property information can be found quickly when needed?
Where is property information currently stored?
options: Shared drive / SharePoint / Google Drive / Dropbox

questions.label: Have you ever discovered an important issue later than you would have liked?
questions.help: An overdue inspection, an expiring certificate, a maintenance issue, a component nearing replacement, a missing document, an unexpected major expense.

questions.label: If yes, what happened?
questions.placeholder: One or two lines is plenty.

questions.label: How useful would it be to have one place that automatically connects documents, building assets, obligations and deadlines, risks and issues, actions and projects, and costs and capital planning?
If the system showed "what needs attention now", what would you most want it to identify?
options: Building components or assets at risk

questions.label: Would a 1–3 year view of likely major property or capital attention be useful?
What decisions would you use that view for?
If AI extracted information from documents or suggested risks and actions, which would you prefer?
options: AI should suggest changes and a person confirms them
I would not trust AI for this

questions.label: How important is it that every important recommendation shows where the information came from — the document, inspection, quote or other evidence?
How valuable would these capabilities be?
rows: One calendar for inspections, obligations, maintenance and major work
Assigning actions to staff and vendors
Reminders and escalation for important items
Evidence showing that work was actually completed

questions.label: If you could fix one property-management problem with technology tomorrow, what would it be?
What software do you use today, and what do you like or dislike about it?
If I had an early version of this product, would you be willing to:
options: Introduce me to another property manager, council member or investor
